perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- He is Gary’s long-time friend from middle school; they have maintained a close friendship and often rely on each other for support.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation. He heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. He suspected Gary’s overworking involved more than just professional obligations.
- He told Gary they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything; he was there to help, not judge. He heard Gary reply that it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden him.
- Gary then opened up to him about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. He heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and remaining challenges, and offered support and encouragement. He heard Gary say things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie.
- Ethan felt hopeful and proud of Gary’s progress.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary as capable of managing on his own and believed Gary had reached a healthier work-life balance. He felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away, knew Gary had this, and should keep up the good work.
- He heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control.
